segments.text: First, the code. SerpAID is fully open source on GitHub under the MIT license. A deterministic WHO protocol engine, a Strands multi-agent graph on Amazon Nova, and a tested guarantee that the model can never recommend a harmful action.

Use case one. A caller in India is about to tie a tight tourniquet and rush to a village healer, and the victim's eyelids feel heavy. Watch SerpAID catch the tourniquet myth, flag the danger sign, and answer out loud in Hindi.
Use case two. A farm worker, hours from a clinic, has the bite packed in ice. SerpAID ends the wait, says remove the ice and move now, and speaks the answer in Portuguese.
Use case three. A child has trouble breathing while a relative tries to suck the venom out. SerpAID stops the suction, escalates to an emergency, and responds in Spanish.
Use case four. A woman is bitten near a river and the wound keeps bleeding. No myth to correct, but SerpAID keeps the family calm and treats it as the emergency it is, in French.
